clue.text: Salt — tea needs a large quantity

parts.note: maté is a South American herbal tea
a lot is a large quantity

explanation.surface: The tea needs heaps of salt added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' looks like seasoning; an old salt is a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A matelot is British slang for a sailor, as is an old salt.

clue.text: Talk to midshipman in illegal premises

parts.note: to talk is to speak
Mr Midshipman Easy is the hero of Captain Marryat's novel

explanation.surface: Have a word with a junior naval officer in a shady drinking den.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Midshipman Easy is an 1836 novel by Frederick Marryat.
explanation.definitionFit: During American Prohibition a bar selling liquor illicitly was so called.

clue.text: Gangster with weapon causes apprehension

parts.note: Al Capone is the archetypal gangster
an arm is a weapon

explanation.surface: An armed mobster spreads fear.
explanation.definitionFit: Fear and anxiety at sensed danger are both senses of the word.

clue.text: Enid gets a different name

indicators.note: different means the letters of Enid gets a are formed into another order

explanation.surface: A woman called Enid is given a new name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'name' looks like a noun but is the verb, meaning to appoint.
explanation.definitionFit: To designate someone is to nominate or appoint them.

clue.text: Task given as punishment to fag

explanation.surface: A schoolboy servant is set a chore as a penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: FAG is British slang for a wearisome chore, and also a junior boy who served a senior at a public school, which colours the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: In the army a menial duty imposed as a penalty is so called; and British slang for tiring toil is a fag.

clue.text: Country not using English money

indicators.note: not using means a letter is dropped from the country's name

parts.note: France is a country

explanation.surface: A nation refuses to accept sterling.
explanation.definitionFit: The former French currency unit was a sum of money.

clue.text: Ditch worker showing vigour

parts.note: a trench is a ditch
a worker ant is the crossword's usual worker

explanation.surface: A labourer digging a ditch works with energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Incisive and forceful speech or criticism is vigorous and cutting.

clue.text: Train a new union member

explanation.surface: Preparing a young recruit to the trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' looks like a trade union, but it is a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: To prepare or coach someone is to groom them; a bridegroom has just joined a marriage.

clue.text: Board up pictures inspired by Muses

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the whole thing is read from the bottom upwards
inspired by means the pictures are breathed into, so placed inside, the Muses

parts.note: there were nine Muses
pictures collectively are art

explanation.surface: Climbing aboard to view paintings the Muses inspired.
explanation.walkthrough: ART inside NINE gives NIARTNE; 'up' reverses it in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To get on a train is to board it.

clue.text: A foreign character at the assembly

indicators.note: assembly means putting the letters of the words at the together in a new order

explanation.surface: An outsider turns up at a public meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembly' reads as a gathering of people, but it is the signal to assemble the letters of AT THE afresh.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a letter of the Greek alphabet, a character from a foreign script.

clue.text: He carries the can once to avoid attack

parts.note: scape is an archaic (once used) form of escape, meaning to avoid
to go at someone is to attack them

explanation.surface: Someone takes the blame, as he formerly dodged an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' flags an old word: SCAPE was formerly used for escape. The attack is read as two words, GO AT. To carry the can is British slang for taking the blame.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who carries the can takes blame for others, the role of a fall guy.

clue.text: In staggering lick, one match is over very quickly

indicators.note: staggering suggests a reeling, unsteady arrangement, so these letters are thrown into new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a match is a game

explanation.surface: A boxer's staggering blow means the bout ends in no time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In staggering' signals reshuffling LICK, I and GAME together; 'is over' just links them to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens as if by sorcery happens at once, instantly and effortlessly.

clue.text: Pause, lying back in middle of bed

indicators.note: lying back indicates the remaining letters are read in reverse order
only the middle of the bed's name is used, its outer letters dropped

parts.note: a hammock is a hanging bed

explanation.surface: Someone takes a break, reclining in the centre of the mattress.
explanation.walkthrough: The bed is a HAMMOCK; 'middle of' strips H and K to give AMMOC, and 'lying back' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: This punctuation mark marks a short break in a sentence.

clue.text: Form of transport — quiet boat

parts.note: a tram is a form of public transport on rails
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A travel option: a silent vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: A tramp steamer is a cargo ship with no fixed route.
explanation.definitionFit: A cargo vessel that sails wherever trade takes it is so called.

clue.text: It enables one to look over a fairy room

definitions.text: It enables one to look over

parts.note: a peri is a fairy of Persian myth
scope is room to manoeuvre

explanation.surface: A device lets you peep into a fairy's chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: A submarine's tube with mirrors lets the viewer see above a barrier.

clue.text: A party share in worship

parts.note: a do is a party
a ration is a fixed share

explanation.surface: A gathering where everyone gets a portion during a religious service.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep reverent love and veneration is a synonym for worship.

clue.text: Regulation number one in the artillery

indicators.note: in means the number is placed within the word for artillery

parts.note: ordnance is artillery, heavy guns
number one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: The leading rule among gunners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number one' reads as the top rule; it is just I.
explanation.definitionFit: A municipal rule or decree is a regulation.

clue.text: Extensively and enthusiastically …

explanation.surface: Doing something both widely and with gusto.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots lead into the next clue but play no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means on a large scale, and also with great zeal.

clue.text: Steady when fired on by mistake

indicators.note: mistake shows the letters of fired on by have been put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Keeping calm when friendly fire comes your way by accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by mistake' looks like a phrase, but 'by' is part of the fodder FIRED ON BY and 'mistake' alone is the signal; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular partner, in informal speech, is one's steady.

clue.text: … plot mischief and plague

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot
evil is harm, mischief

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue: scheming wrongdoing and torment on a grand scale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' looks like a verb, scheme; it is a flower bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedevil is to torment or harass persistently.

clue.text: Left the spot about to go fishing

indicators.note: about means the combined letters are turned round

parts.note: a wart is a spot or blemish on the skin

explanation.surface: Someone quit the place, ready to head off with rod and line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the whole of L plus WART, giving the answer back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: To drag a large net through the sea is to fish in a particular way.

clue.text: Got to know poet by a diminutive of his name

parts.note: Edward Lear was the nonsense poet
Ned is a pet form of Edward

explanation.surface: Discovered a poet by his nickname.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Lear wrote nonsense verse; Ned is short for Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: To find out a fact is to come to know it.

clue.text: Young girl gets America alight

parts.note: a deb is a debutante, a young girl entering society

explanation.surface: A girl sets the United States on fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alight' looks like 'on fire'; it means to get off a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: To get off a bus, as passengers do, is to alight.

clue.text: A scholar and a politician

explanation.surface: Someone is both an academic and a statesman.
explanation.walkthrough: Roger Bacon was a medieval scholar; Francis Bacon was Lord Chancellor.
explanation.definitionFit: Roger the friar was a learned philosopher, and Francis the lord chancellor was a statesman.

clue.text: Steal a friend's crockery

parts.note: bone is slang for steal
china is rhyming slang (china plate = mate) for a friend

explanation.surface: Pinching a pal's plates and cups.
explanation.walkthrough: China plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate; BONE is old slang for steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine translucent porcelain used for tableware is a kind of crockery.

clue.text: Drunk — curse the binge

explanation.surface: A drunk swears about the drinking spree.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a blind is a drinking bout, and 'effing and blinding' means swearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang uses the word for paralytic, for swearing, and for a drinking spree.

clue.text: A lot of soldiers take heart, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals a word that sounds like this one

parts.note: to core an apple is to take its heart out

explanation.surface: Troops are encouraged, so reports say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take heart' reads as be encouraged; it is the verb to core.
explanation.definitionFit: A military unit of troops is a body of soldiers.

clue.text: Two men from Australia

parts.note: Victor is a man's name
Ian is another man's name

explanation.surface: A pair of blokes who have come from Down Under.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria is an Australian state, so a native of it is from Australia; the word also suggests the Queen's era.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the state of Victoria comes from the south-east of that country.

clue.text: It's ashen, or possibly ashy

indicators.note: possibly means the two letters of or may be arranged the other way

parts.note: ashy means pale, wan

explanation.surface: Something looks grey, or perhaps the colour of ash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ashen' reads as pale, but means 'an ash': the mountain ash tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The mountain ash is another name for this tree with red berries.

clue.text: A flax product processed in Leeds

indicators.note: processed means the letters of in Leeds are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire mill turns flax into a commodity.
explanation.walkthrough: Leeds is a northern English city once known for its textile mills.
explanation.definitionFit: Flax seed, pressed for oil, is the plant's best-known product.

clue.text: Tried to look round a ship a day.

indicators.note: round means the word for look goes around the other letters

parts.note: to eye is to look at
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: Someone attempted to inspect a vessel each day.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'a' is a link; the second gives A, which goes with SS inside EYE.
explanation.definitionFit: To essay something is to attempt it.
